title: Multiplying up to 4-Digit Numbers by 1-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Grade 4 Multiplying by 1-Digit Numbers Worksheets: up to 4 Digits (TEKS 4.4D, STAAR)
standard_text: 4.4D use strategies and algorithms, including the standard algorithm, to multiply up to a four-digit number by a one-digit number and to multiply a two-digit number by a two-digit number
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 multiplication worksheets for Texas TEKS 4.4D: multiply 2-, 3- and 4-digit numbers by 1-digit numbers with area models, partial products and the standard algorithm, and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Multiply each place, then add the partial products.
key_sub: In the standard algorithm, start with the ones and add each regrouped digit to the next product.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Break the bigger number into place values: 3,427 = 3,000 + 400 + 20 + 7.
  • Multiply each part by the 1-digit number and add the partial products.
  • In the standard algorithm, multiply from the ones place. Regroup and add the regrouped digit to the next product.
  • Estimate first: 6 × 3,427 is about 6 × 3,000 = 18,000.

Examples

Example

6 × 3,427

6 × 3,000 = 18,000

6 × 400 = 2,400

6 × 20 = 120

6 × 7 = 42

18,000 + 2,400 + 120 + 42

Answer: 20,562

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting a regrouped digitWrite it above the next place and add it after you multiply.
Multiplying only some placesEvery digit is multiplied by the 1-digit number.
Lining up partial products wronglyLine up by place value before adding.

faq.a: Use strategies and algorithms, including the standard algorithm, to multiply up to a four-digit number by a one-digit number.
The products of each place value part, such as 6 × 400 = 2,400. Their sum is the full product.

faq.q: How do I check my answer?
faq.a: Estimate by rounding the bigger number. 6 × 3,427 should be close to 6 × 3,000 = 18,000.

faq.q: What if there is a zero in the number?
faq.a: That place gives a partial product of 0, but keep the place in the standard algorithm.
